testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: During a static leakage test, a single vehicle with air brakes should lose no more than ____ of air pressure in one minute.
questions.explanation: A single vehicle with air brakes should lose no more than 2 psi of air pressure in one minute during a static leakage test. If the system leaks faster than this, the vehicle needs repairs and should not be driven.

questions.question: What type of brakes do most newer heavy-duty trucks have?
questions.explanation: Most newer heavy-duty trucks use dual air brake systems. This system has two separate air brake systems that share one set of brake controls.

questions.question: A low air pressure warning signal:

options.text: Is not recommended on vehicles with air brakes.
Is required on vehicles with air brakes.
Is optional on vehicles with air brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is required on vehicles with air brakes.
questions.explanation: All vehicles with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning signal.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).

questions.question: On a truck with air brakes, the air compressor:

options.text: Pumps air into the air storage tanks.
Moves air to the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pumps air into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks. The air compressor governor controls when the compressor runs.

questions.question: When the brake pedal is pressed and the S-cam turns, the S-cam:

options.text: Presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
Tightens the brake drum onto the axle.
Presses the brake lining against the wheel.
Releases air from the air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: When the brake pedal is pressed and the S-cam turns, it presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum. This creates friction and slows the vehicle.

questions.question: Having ABS on only one axle:

options.text: Still gives you more control when braking.
Slows the vehicle, but cannot stop it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Still gives you more control when braking.
questions.explanation: If ABS is on only the tractor, only the trailer, or only one axle, you will still have better control when braking than without ABS. Brake normally.

questions.question: Brake linings should be:
questions.explanation: Brake linings should be free of oil and grease. They should not be loose or too thin.

questions.question: In S-cam brakes, air pressure added to the brake chambers moves the rods and slack adjusters. This air pressure is added when the driver:
questions.explanation: When the brake pedal is pressed, air enters the brake chambers. This air pressure pushes out the rods and moves the slack adjusters, which turn the brake camshafts.

questions.question: If the ABS warning light comes on while driving, it means:

options.text: The ABS has just been activated.
The ABS is not working properly.
The ABS needs to be activated.

questions.correctAnswerText: The ABS is not working properly.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with ABS have yellow warning lights. If these lights come on, something is wrong with the braking system. You may have lost ABS on one or more wheels.

questions.question: Brake fading happens when:

options.text: Brakes are not used often enough.

questions.explanation: Excessive braking causes brakes to overheat. When brakes overheat, they become less effective. This is called brake fading.

questions.question: Air tank drains should:

options.text: Not be used by the driver.
Only be used when it is wet outside.
Be used to drain the tanks completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be used to drain the tanks completely.
questions.explanation: Compressed air in air brake systems contains water and compressor oil. This water and oil can damage the brakes if they build up in the system. Open manual air tank drains every day to remove this buildup.

questions.question: Alcohol evaporators:

options.text: Add alcohol to braking systems to prevent freezing.
Are only allowed on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Add alcohol to braking systems to prevent freezing.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. It adds alcohol to the braking system to stop ice from forming, which can cause damage.

questions.question: When only the tractor has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: There is a decreased risk of jackknifing.
There is an increased risk of jackknifing.
The brakes will not work as well without ABS.
The brakes will become more sensitive.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a decreased risk of jackknifing.
questions.explanation: When a tractor has ABS but the trailer does not, the risk of jackknifing decreases. The driver can still steer and maintain control. If only the trailer has ABS, the trailer is less likely to swing out.

questions.question: If the low air pressure warning signal comes on in a vehicle with air brakes, the driver should:

options.text: Test the brakes while driving and continue if nothing seems wrong.

questions.explanation: When the low air pressure warning signal comes on, stop and park safely as soon as possible. You need to stop while you still have some braking power left.

questions.question: How many air storage tanks does an air brake system use?
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold compressed air. Different vehicles have different numbers and sizes of air tanks in their air brake systems.

questions.question: Air pressure should build up in a single air system within:
questions.explanation: In a single air brake system, once the engine reaches operating speed, pressure should build from 50 to 90 psi within three minutes.

questions.question: A low air pressure warning signal must activate when:
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, the low air pressure warning signal must come on when tank pressure falls below 60 psi. The warning may be a light, buzzer, or wig wag.

questions.question: To stop a vehicle using air brakes:
questions.explanation: To stop normally in a vehicle with air brakes, press down on the brake pedal.

questions.question: Manual air tank drains should be:

options.text: Opened to drain the tanks after each day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Opened to drain the tanks after each day.
questions.explanation: Compressed air in air brake systems contains water and compressor oil. This water and oil can damage the brakes if they build up. Open manual air tank drains every day to remove this buildup.

questions.question: While driving, spring brakes are held in place by:
questions.explanation: While driving, spring brakes are held in place by air pressure. When air pressure drops low enough, the springs activate the brakes.

questions.question: A slack adjuster should move no more than ____ from where it is attached to the push rod.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check each slack adjuster. Park the vehicle, set wheel chocks, and disengage the parking brake. Pull the slack adjusters to make sure they do not move more than one inch from where the push rod is attached. If they move more than one inch, they need to be fixed.

questions.question: When inspecting your brakes, a slack adjuster should move ____ from where it is attached to the push rod.
questions.explanation: Check each slack adjuster by setting wheel chocks and disengaging the parking brake. Pull the slack adjusters to make sure they do not move more than one inch from where the push rod is attached. If they move more than one inch, they need to be fixed.

questions.question: To confirm that a trailer has ABS, you can:

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors coming from the back of the brakes.
Look under the hood for the ABS sticker.
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors coming from the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: To check if a trailer has Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), look under the vehicle for the electronic control unit and wheel speed sensor wires coming from the back of the brakes.

questions.question: You must have an air brake endorsement:

options.text: To use a vehicle with air brakes.
To drive any truck with a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: To use a vehicle with air brakes.
questions.explanation: You must pass an air brakes knowledge test to get a license to operate a vehicle with air brakes, including an air over hydraulic braking system.
